cards.definition: The overall field of making machines perform tasks that need intelligence.
cards.useCase: Use it for the whole field; machine learning is one approach within it.
cards.example: A hand-written rule engine and a learned model are both AI

cards.definition: An approach to AI in which a system learns rules from data instead of being given them.
cards.useCase: Use it when the rules are too many or too hard to write by hand.
cards.example: Learning to spot spam from labelled emails

cards.definition: The collection of examples an algorithm learns from.
cards.useCase: Fit the model to it; keep a separate test set aside.
cards.example: 10,000 emails marked spam or not spam

cards.definition: What a training algorithm produces: the learned relationship used to make predictions.
cards.useCase: Apply it to new inputs to get predictions.
cards.example: A trained line that maps floor area to price

cards.definition: An input variable that describes each example.
cards.useCase: Choose features that carry information about the target.
cards.example: Floor area, bedrooms, age of a house

cards.definition: The value the model is trained to predict. Also called the label or the 'answer'.
cards.useCase: It is what supervised learning is given and tries to reproduce.
cards.example: The sale price of the house

cards.definition: Learning from data whose labels (the answers) are given.
cards.useCase: Use it when you have examples with known outcomes.
cards.example: Emails marked spam or not spam

cards.definition: Learning from data with no labels; the algorithm looks for structure by itself.
cards.useCase: Use it to find groups or patterns you did not name in advance.
cards.example: Finding natural groups of shoppers

cards.definition: Learning from feedback (rewards and penalties) that an environment gives in response to actions.
cards.useCase: Use it for sequential decisions such as games and robots.
cards.example: A program rewarded with points for scoring

cards.definition: The known answer attached to a training example.
cards.useCase: Its presence is what makes learning supervised.
cards.example: A photo tagged 'cat'

cards.definition: Supervised learning where the target is a category from a discrete, fixed set.
cards.useCase: Use it when the answer is a class such as yes or no.
cards.example: Dog or not dog; spam or not spam

cards.definition: Supervised learning where the target is a continuous value with infinitely many possibilities.
cards.useCase: Use it when the answer is a number on a scale.
cards.example: A house price; tomorrow's temperature

cards.definition: A classifier that labels a new example by looking at the labels of its k closest training examples.
cards.useCase: A simple supervised method for classification.
cards.example: Classify a fruit by its 5 nearest neighbours

cards.definition: Supervised models that classify by following a series of questions; a random forest combines many trees.
cards.useCase: Classification when you want an easy-to-read set of rules.
cards.example: Is the age over 30? -> Is the income over 50k? -> ...

cards.definition: A regression method that fits a line to predict a continuous value.
cards.useCase: Predict numbers such as prices.
cards.example: price = slope x area + intercept

cards.definition: Despite the name, almost always used for binary classification, giving a probability of one class.
cards.useCase: Yes or no predictions such as fraud or not.
cards.example: Probability that a customer will cancel

cards.definition: Grouping unlabelled examples so that similar ones are together. An unsupervised task.
cards.useCase: Find natural groups when none are named.
cards.example: Customer segments

cards.definition: A clustering algorithm that places k centroids at random, then repeatedly assigns points to the nearest centroid and moves each centroid to the centre of its points.
cards.useCase: Cluster data into a chosen number of groups.
cards.example: k = 4 gives four customer segments

cards.definition: The hyperparameter for the number of clusters you want the algorithm to find.
cards.useCase: You choose it before training.

cards.definition: The centre of a cluster. k-means starts them at random positions and moves them to fit the data.
cards.useCase: It represents a cluster; its position is learned.
cards.example: Centre of the 'big spenders' group

cards.definition: A variable inside the model that the training algorithm sets while learning from data.
cards.useCase: Learned, not chosen.
cards.example: Slope and intercept of a fitted line

cards.definition: A configuration of the training algorithm that we set ourselves, before training.
cards.useCase: Chosen by us, then tuned.
cards.example: k in k-means; neighbours in kNN

cards.definition: The number of correct predictions divided by the total number of samples.
cards.useCase: A one-number summary of how often the model is right.

cards.definition: A grid comparing actual classes with predicted classes. Correct predictions lie on the diagonal.
cards.useCase: See which classes get mistaken for which.
cards.example: 40 cats right, 10 cats called dogs, 5 dogs called cats, 45 dogs right

cards.definition: How well a model performs on unseen examples that were not in its training set.
cards.useCase: It is what we really care about; measure it on test data.
cards.example: Test accuracy

cards.definition: Accuracy measured on the data the model was trained with.
cards.useCase: Compare it with test accuracy.
cards.example: 99% on training data

cards.definition: Accuracy measured on data held back from training.
cards.useCase: Shows how well the model generalizes.
cards.example: 62% on test data

cards.definition: The model memorizes the training set. It has high variance and low bias, with high training accuracy and low test accuracy.
cards.useCase: Spot it by a large gap between training and test accuracy.
cards.example: Train 99%, test 62%

cards.definition: The model is too simple to capture the complexity of the data. It has high bias and low variance, with low training accuracy.
cards.useCase: Spot it by poor accuracy on the training data too.
cards.example: Train 55%, test 54%

cards.definition: Error from a model that is too simple. High bias goes with underfitting.
cards.useCase: Too much means the model misses the pattern.
cards.example: A straight line through curved data

cards.definition: Error from a model that is too sensitive to the particular training examples. High variance goes with overfitting.
cards.useCase: Too much means the model does not carry over to new data.
cards.example: A model that changes a lot with each training set
